description: Stage 4 rewrites the second conjunct with a claim Replay does not recognize as movement, and also builds an ordinary new head (C[E]) and its C′ around existing material. The new head must be selected and merged before the rewrite moment, not appear at the stage record.
source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run, 17 October 2026 (rare-relations batch, 15-dutch-stripping, analysis 1).
sentence: Jan heeft een boek gekocht en Marie ook.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The first clause means that Jan has bought a book. The second reconstructs the same predicate with Marie as its subject. In this classical GB implementation, external arguments originate in Spec-IP; Dutch VP and I-bar are head-final. Each occurrence of gekocht assigns its external Agent role to the corresponding subject and its Theme role to its object. Finite heeft licenses nominative Case on the subject, and gekocht assigns accusative Case to the object. Each auxiliary selects a participial VP and contributes perfect interpretation. The second clause's repeated predicate is represented explicitly but has not yet received a surface realization or undergone deletion. Its indefinite need not denote the same book as the first clause's indefinite. The conjunction and additive particle are separate lexical objects at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the two underlying clauses for the subject-remnant reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A finite CP is projected over each IP, and heeft moves from I to C in each clause. This establishes the verbal component of Dutch verb-second order before either preverbal position is filled. Each vacated I position is a silent head trace linked to its raised auxiliary; the Case and agreement properties established through I remain available through that head chain. The second auxiliary is reconstructed syntax, not an additional input token.
derivationStages.statement: Raise both finite auxiliaries into the finite C positions.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Jan moves from the first Spec-IP to Spec-CP, producing Jan heeft followed by the head-final predicate. Marie independently moves from the second Spec-IP to its finite Spec-CP. Her movement is the first step of remnant evacuation, not deletion. Both are A-bar chains whose lower subject positions retain the external theta roles and nominative Case established earlier. The Spec-CP occurrences locally antecedent-govern their subject traces. The nominal lexical subtrees move with the pronounced occurrences; the source positions contain traces rather than additional pronounced names.
derivationStages.statement: Front Jan and move the second subject through the finite CP edge.

values.meaning: Marie is an additional individual satisfying the recovered predicate

derivationStages.stageRecord: The second conjunct receives a higher focus CP, an articulated extension of the clause's left periphery. Its silent C carries an ellipsis feature. Ook heads a particle projection between that C and the lower finite CP. Marie now moves from the already established finite Spec-CP to the higher Spec-CP, leaving an intermediate trace. The resulting successive-cyclic chain connects the high remnant, the finite CP edge, and the subject position without skipping a clausal escape position. Ook associates with the high Marie constituent and will therefore survive deletion with it. This outer focus shell is required because deleting only IP after ordinary V2 movement would incorrectly leave the second heeft pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Place Marie and ook outside the prospective deletion domain.

values.reading: Jan has bought a book, and Marie has bought a book too
values.sharedAbstraction: the property of having bought a book

derivationStages.stageRecord: The ellipsis-bearing higher C licenses nonpronunciation of the entire lower finite CP, including the raised second auxiliary, the reconstructed object and participle, and all lower traces. Deletion follows remnant evacuation: Marie and ook are already outside that CP. Recovery compares the two clauses after abstracting over their contrasting subjects; both supply the property of having bought a book. The indefinite is interpreted within each buying proposition, so this reading does not require Jan and Marie to have bought one identical book. The conjunction combines the overt first CP and the reduced second focus CP as clausal conjuncts. This is stripping, not merely VP ellipsis: the second finite auxiliary is absent as well. The retained theta, Case, and movement chains interpret Marie as the buyer. The final pronounced order is exactly Jan heeft een boek gekocht en Marie ook.
derivationStages.statement: Complete clausal coordination and subject-oriented stripping.
